newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: World Bank says will overtake IMF in Russia loans.
newsitem.headline: World Bank says will overtake IMF in Russia loans.

text.p: World Bank chief James Wolfensohn praised Russian President Boris Yeltsin's economic reforms on Thursday and predicted his agency would soon take over from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) as the main lender to Moscow.
The bank relaxed the purse strings for Russia and approved loans worth nearly $885 million last week. It says it could lend as much as $6 billion in the next two years if reforms stick.

"The IMF is doing 10 billion dollars over three years. We're coming in with a programme which is about the same. If they finish, we're going to be the big lender," Wolfensohn told a news conference in Geneva.
"If they (IMF) don't decide to lend anymore, then we will become more important in lending (to Russia) than the IMF."
The IMF has a three-year $10.2 billion budget support loan for Russia which was agreed in 1996.
Wolfensohn said the bank was happy with reforms carried out by Yeltsin's team. He said 90 percent of the bank's loans would go towards the financing of social programmes in Russia.
"With regard to Russia, we have formed a judgement. That is the current team under President Yeltsin...have come up with programmes that are socially responsible," he said.

"I am well aware that there are critics. But we have formed the view that this team is legitimately trying to address the social problems. Our objective is to ensure that the funds that we're providing do reach the people."
